title: Per-technology query decomposition and evidence-sufficiency gate
hypothesis: Technology-specific subqueries improve canonical evidence retrieval, while requiring eligible evidence from both technology sides reduces comparative false positives.

variants.description: Current balanced retrieval over one comparative query; answer when any chunk passes.
Retrieve independently with one frozen subquery per technology and retain up to two chunks per side; answer when either side passes.
Use the same decomposed candidates but return evidence only when both technology sides have at least one chunk above threshold.

changedVariable: Comparative query execution and evidence-sufficiency decision architecture
controlledVariables: eight comparative positives and eight comparative negatives
maximum two chunks per technology for decomposed variants

selectionRule.failurePolicy: Select no architecture when no candidate satisfies every guardrail; do not tune subquery wording or the gate after observing results.

execution.interpretation: Per-technology decomposition improves two-sided retrieval. The both-sides gate is necessary: without it the same decomposed candidates produce 0.50 negative FPR, while the gate rejects all eight negatives and no positives.
